messages.subject: Recent updates to Rattle (Version 2.3.45) and PMML (Version 1.1.9)
messages.subject_clean: Recent updates to Rattle (Version 2.3.45) and PMML (Version 1.1.9)
messages.body_plain:
Time for another update on progress with Rattle.

Version 2.3.45 is propagating through CRAN.

Overall details are available from

  http://rattle.togaware.com/changes.html

As always, you can install the beta version with:

  > install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com")

This release includes PMML updates from Zementis for decision trees.
PMML output for predictive models is getting a lot better thanks to
Zementis. Their web based PMML tools (e.g., http://www.zementis.com/pmml_converters.htm)
work well with models generated from Rattle.

Regards,
Graham

On May 28, 5:54 am, Graham Williams <Graham.Willi...@togaware.com>
wrote:

> I have some very basic experimental code - but not yet useful. There
> are problems in exporting some models to SQL. In particular, ensembles
> generate very large SQL.
>
> The PMML, in theory, can be loaded into Teradata Warehouse Miner which
> will convert it to SQL. I've successfully tested this with single
> decision trees.
>
> I'm looking at exporting to PMML and C++ code in the near future. I
> would imagine that pretty much the same parsing can be used to
> generate SQL. Happy for anyone to contribute code to do so :-)
>
> I have the C++ export working for randomForests (and we've done some
> basic testing to show that a 500 tree forest exported as C++ can score
> 12 million rows of transactions in about 60 seconds on a Netezza data
> warehouse.)
>
> The proper solution would be to write a package to read PMML and
> convert that to C++ or SQL. The short term solution will be to model
> the C++ and SQL code generation on the PMML generating code in the
> pmml package. Shouldn't be too hard......
>
> Regards,
> Graham

SQL?

********************************************************************
                2nd Call for Papers - DDDM 2008
    The 2nd International Workshop on Domain Driven Data Mining
                 Pisa, Italy, December 15, 2008
                In conjunction with IEEE ICDM'08
          URL: http://datamining.it.uts.edu.au/dddm08/
********************************************************************

The Second International Workshop on Domain Driven Data Mining
(DDDM 2008) aims to provide a premier forum for sharing findings,
knowledge, insight, experience and lessons in tackling potential
challenges in discovering actionable knowledge from complex domain
problems, promote the interaction of and fill the gap between data
mining research and business expectations, and drive a paradigm
shift from traditional data-centered hidden pattern mining to
domain-driven actionable knowledge discovery.

Submission Instructions
-----------------------
Paper submissions should be limited to a maximum of 10 pages in the
IEEE 2-column format, the same as the camera-ready format (see the
IEEE Computer Society Press Proceedings Author Guidelines at
http://www.computer.org/portal/pages/cscps/cps/final/icdm06.xml).
All papers accepted for the workshop will be included in the
ICDM'08 Workshop Proceedings published by the IEEE Computer Society
Press. Selected papers from the workshop will be invited for
consideration of publication in a planned special issue of IEEE
Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (subject to approval
from TKDE).

Important dates
---------------
  August 1, 2008:          Submission deadline
  September 15, 2008:      Notification of paper acceptance to authors
  October 7, 2008:         Deadline for camera-ready copies
  December 15, 2008:       Workshop day

messages.subject: Re: Export to SQL
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

It is very convient to have the models run inside a centralised
customer database/datawharehouse, this is why a number of high-end
database systems have PMML support built in.  If you are not running
one of these particular DBs that have PMML built in, it would
therefore be helpful to have SQL version of the model/s.

Scoring externally to the company does not suit my needs as I am
unable to transfer sensitive customer data outside of the
organisation.

Regards,
Shane

messages.subject: Re: Export to SQL
messages.body_plain:
SQL for some models is quite a problem - We considered a randomForest
with 500 trees, each tree about 10, with something like 180 leaf
nodes. A naive conversion to SQL would be about 500*10*180 or 900,000
lines. (Considerable simplification possible, but still quite a lot of
SQL.) Even data warehouse systems can't cope.

We did some testing converting the randomForest into C code and
running that on a newer to market data warehouse. Applying this model
to some 10 million entities took less than 2 minutes.

SQL might work for simple models, and that might be all you need.

Regards,
Graham

scoring system that can support that, is scalable, and allows for fast
deployment of different predictive strategies is a need in many
industries.

Alex

messages.subject: Re: Export to SQL
messages.body_plain:
I agree there may potentially be some difficulties in converting
particular models to SQL.  Where it is possible though I think there
are big wins in terms of portability and ease of deployment...

Graham's approach of converting to C is interesting (and speedy by the
sounds of it!).  Another approach could be to implement in the
database's procedural language.  For example, PostgreSQL supports
several languages including Perl, Python and even R!

Cheers,
Shane

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

There is a problem with the fBasics package that causes an error when
running rattle. I just did a test on the audit dataset using rattle
2.3.50, and using an updated fBasics package 260.72 and it worked fine for me.

My advice to you is to update fBasics package, and then run it
separate from the summary option, under the explore tab. If it works
then try running both the summary and basics options under the explore tab.

Regards
Tony

messages.subject: Exploratory Data Analysis using Rattle
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I have a data set that consists of remote sensing spectral data and
associated lidar metrics. The spectral data consists of 4m resolution
blue, green, red, and near-IR spectra, while the lidar data consists
of various lidar metrics derived from a top of canopy point cloud. My
aim is to explore what relationships exist between the spectral data
and the lidar metrics and use these relationships in further analysis.
The idea behind the project is to develop an optimal lidar sampling
scheme for forest structural assessment.

What are your thoughts on the matter and do you think that Rattle is
suitable for exploratory data analysis. If not could you point me
towards a suitable replacement.

Many thanks and kind regards,
Wesley

and select KMeans and score, then execute. Currently working on making
this work with any specified dataset.
